problems.title: Integrate a doubled-angle cosine
problems.question: Evaluate ∫cos(2x)dx from π/12 toπ/4.
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
steps: The endpoint difference is (sin(π/2)−sin(π/6))/2=(1−1/2)/2=1/4.

problems.title: A constant term has derivative zero
problems.question: Find f′(7π/6) if f(x)=sin(3π/7)+cos(3x/7).
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
steps: The first sine is constant. At the given input,the second sine’s argument isπ/2,so f′=−3/7.

problems.title: A radical comparison with negative inputs
problems.question: Solve x−√(3−2x)<0.
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
formulas: Domain x≤3/2; for x<0 the inequality x<√(3−2x) is automatic.
steps: For x≥0,square to obtain x²<3−2x,or (x+3)(x−1)<0. This gives0≤x<1.
Combining with all negative inputs gives x<1. The endpoint1 is excluded because it gives equality.

problems.title: Directrices of an ellipse
problems.question: Find distance between directrices of x²/48+y²/12=1.
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
steps: Substitute a²=48,c=6: distance=96/6=16.

problems.title: Parabola from its focus
problems.question: A parabola has vertex (0,0) and focus (3,0). Find its equation.
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
steps: Here p=3,so y²=12x. Its directrix is x=−3,consistent with the vertex midway between focus and directrix.

problems.title: A logarithm-base substitution
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of x·2^(log_x5)=10.
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
formulas: Domain x>0,x≠1. Let t=log₂x; then log_x5=log₂5/t.
steps: Taking log₂ gives t+(log₂5)/t=1+log₂5.
Multiplication by t gives (t−1)(t−log₂5)=0. Thus x=2 or5,both valid. Their sum is7.

problems.title: Use a derivative inside an equation
problems.question: Solve √(2x+18)=√f′(1),where f=(x²−3x)⁴.
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
steps: At x=1,the derivative is4·(−2)³·(−1)=32.
Both sides are nonnegative,so equality of square roots is equivalent to2x+18=32. Thus x=7,which satisfies the domain.

problems.title: A standard exponential limit
problems.question: Find lim as x→∞ of [(x+5)/(x−7)]^x.
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
formulas: Write the base as 1+12/(x−7),and use $(1+c/t)^t\to e^c$.
steps: Putting t=x−7 gives (1+12/t)^(t+7). Its t-power tends to e¹² and its extra seventh power tends to1.

problems.title: Cosine of the angle between planes
problems.question: Find cosine of the angle between 11x−8y−7z+5=0 and7x+2y−8z−3=0.
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
steps: Use normals (11,−8,−7) and(7,2,−8). Their dot product is77−16+56=117.
Their squared lengths are234 and117,so the cosine is117/√(234·117)=1/√2.

problems.title: Rotate a right triangle about its hypotenuse
problems.question: Rotate a triangle of sides3,4,5 around its longest side. Find surface area.
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
formulas: The altitude to the hypotenuse is h=3·4/5=12/5. Two cones share this radius; their slant lengths are3 and4.
steps: Only the two cone lateral surfaces are exposed. Total area=πh(3+4)=π·(12/5)·7=84π/5.

problems.title: A logarithmic inequality with incompatible conditions
problems.question: Solve ln(2·4^x−8·2^x)≤ln(2^x−4).
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
formulas: Let t=2^x>0. Both logarithm arguments require t>4.
steps: The increasing logarithm allows comparison:2t²−8t≤t−4,or (2t−1)(t−4)≤0.
This requires1/2≤t≤4,which has no overlap with the strict domain t>4. Thus there are no solutions.

problems.title: A tangent perpendicular to a line
problems.question: Which listed point on f(x)=(x⁴−x²)/4−x³/3 has tangent perpendicular to y=−x/3+8?
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
steps: At x=2,the derivative is8−4−1=3. Also f(2)=(16−4)/4−8/3=1/3.
Thus (2,1/3) is the listed point meeting both requirements.

problems.title: Area between two parabolas
problems.question: Find area between y=−2x²+10x−4 and y=x²−2x+5.
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
steps: The curves meet at x=1,3. Integrate their nonnegative difference on this interval.
With u=x−2,the area is3∫₋₁¹(1−u²)du=3·(2−2/3)=4.

problems.title: Hyperbola from axis and focus lengths
problems.question: A hyperbola has imaginary-axis length6 and distance between foci14. Which listed equation fits?
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
steps: Thus the listed horizontal hyperbola is x²/40−y²/9=1. The full axis lengths,not their halves,were6 and14.

problems.title: Order vertices around a quadrilateral
problems.question: Find the area of the quadrilateral whose vertices are A(1,3),B(4,7),C(−1,−2),D(2,2).
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
formulas: For a parallelogram, area is the absolute determinant of adjacent side vectors.
steps: The boundary order is A,B,D,C. Adjacent vectors from A are AB=(3,4),AC=(−2,−5).
Their determinant is3·(−5)−4·(−2)=−7,so the ordinary quadrilateral area is7.
problems.note: The displayed list is not cyclic boundary order. Joining A,B,C,D in that order creates a crossed figure; the answer uses the ordinary quadrilateral with these four vertices.

problems.title: Zero product on a restricted radical domain
problems.question: Find the sum of all roots of sinx·√(2+3x−2x²)=0.
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
formulas: The radical domain is [−1/2,2]. A product vanishes if either factor is zero.
steps: The radical vanishes at x=−1/2 and2. In the domain,the only sine zero x=kπ is0.
The distinct roots sum to−1/2+0+2=3/2.

problems.title: Check only the piecewise join points
problems.question: How many discontinuities has f=2 for x<−1;2−2x for −1≤x<1;lnx for x≥1?
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
formulas: Each branch is continuous inside its interval. Compare one-sided limits at −1 and1.
steps: At −1,the left limit is2 and the right limit and value are4,so there is a jump.
At1,the left limit is0 and l n1=0,so the branches join continuously. There is exactly one discontinuity.

problems.title: A logarithmic integral by substitution
problems.question: Evaluate ∫x/(x²+2)dx from1 to2.
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
steps: The value is(ln6−ln3)/2=(ln2)/2.

problems.title: A plane containing an entire coordinate axis
problems.question: Plane Ax+By+Cz+D=0 contains Ox and(1,2,3). Find (A+D+B)/C.
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
formulas: All (x,0,0) lie in the plane,so A=D=0. Containment of the point gives2B+3C=0.
steps: Since a valid plane requires a nonzero normal,C cannot be zero. Therefore the requested ratio is B/C=−3/2.

problems.title: Rotate the region under a reciprocal curve
problems.question: Rotate the region bounded by xy=4,x=1,x=4,y=0 about Ox. Find volume.
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
steps: An antiderivative of16/x² is−16/x. Evaluate to getπ(−4+16)=12π.

problems.title: Acceleration from two derivatives
problems.question: Given S(t)=t³−11t,find acceleration when velocity is16 and time is nonnegative.
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
steps: Set3t²−11=16,so t²=9. Nonnegative time gives t=3.
Then acceleration is6·3=18 m/s².

problems.title: An inflection requires a concavity change
problems.question: Which listed x is an inflection of f(x)=(x³−1)/(4x²)?
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
steps: The function is concave downward on both parts of its domain. No point changes concavity.
The excluded input0 is not a graph point and cannot be an inflection point.

problems.title: A slant asymptote from a limiting correction
problems.question: Find the slant asymptote of f(x)=x/2−arccos[2x/(1+x²)].
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
steps: Thus f(x)−(x/2−π/2) tends to zero at both infinities. The asymptote is y=(x−π)/2.

problems.title: External sphere tangent to cone and base plane
problems.question: A cone has equilateral axial section of side4. A sphere touches its side and base plane at D,whose distance from the axis is3. Find sphere radius.
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
formulas: Cone R=2,h=2√3. Its side in an axial plane is √3x+z−2√3=0; point-to-line distance equals the sphere radius.
steps: Let radius beρ,so the centre is(3,ρ). External tangency gives(3√3+ρ−2√3)/2=ρ.
Therefore ρ=√3. The perpendicular foot on the side has coordinates(3/2,√3/2),inside the actual cone generator.

problems.title: Distance between a slanted chord and a generator
problems.question: In a cylinder,AB=12 on one base,B₁C₁=9 on the other,BB₁ is a generator and AC₁ crosses the axis. Find distance between lines AC₁ and BB₁.
problems.idea: Simplify first, keeping the original domain and geometric conditions.
formulas: Project onto the base. Since AC₁ crosses the axis,the projections A,C are opposite circle points. Triangle ABC is right atB.
steps: Its hypotenuse is AC=√(12²+9²)=15. Its altitude from B toAC is12·9/15=7.2.
A horizontal segment perpendicular toAC is perpendicular both to the vertical generator and to the slanted line AC₁. Allowing their infinite lines,its endpoints can be taken at one common height.
Thus this projected altitude is exactly the shortest distance between the two lines.
